title: Slider
summary: A slider allows users to select a value or range of values by moving handles along a track.

columns.content:
Use a slider when users benefit from adjusting a value visually.    
It works well when:

- The value is part of a continuous or stepped range, such as volume, amount or intensity.
- Adjusting and exploring the value is more important than entering a precise number.

The slider can be adjusted using pointer, touch or keyboard.

- Moving the handle updates the value according to the defined step.
- The value indicator displays the current value while the slider is being adjusted.
- The slider should provide immediate visual feedback as the value changes.

A slider can be used to select a single value or a range between two values. Both types can use steps to define the interval between selectable values. Choose a minimum, maximum and step that match the scale and level of precision users need. For example, a slider from 0 to 100 with a step of 5 allows values such as 0, 5, 10 and 15. 

- Single value – uses one handle to select a value between a defined minimum and maximum.
- Range – uses two handles to select a lower and upper value within a defined minimum and maximum.

overview.title: Value display
overview.section-content: By default, the slider includes a textbox that displays the selected value and allows users to enter a precise value. The textbox can be omitted when the selected value or its effect is clearly displayed elsewhere in the interface. For example, adjusting an interest rate could update a monthly cost displayed in a separate summary or card.

columns.title: Textbox
columns.content: For a single-value slider, one textbox displays the selected value. For a range slider, two textboxes display the selected lower and upper values. The slider and textbox should always stay synchronised. Changing the value in either one should update the other.

columns.title: Value indicator
columns.content: A bubble appears next to the handle while the slider is being adjusted. It displays the current value and updates as the handle moves. For a range slider, the value indicator displays the value of the handle currently being adjusted.

overview.title: Accessibility
overview.section-content:
The slider is built on the native HTML , providing built-in semantics and keyboard interaction. A slider must expose its current value, minimum value and maximum value to assistive technologies. This is handled out of the box when using the slider component from Green.

Ensure that:

- The slider has an accessible name describing what the value controls.
- The selected value is communicated through more than the visual position of the handle.

columns.title: Keyboard
columns.content:
When the slider has focus:

- Arrow right / Arrow up increases the value by one step.
- Arrow left / Arrow down decreases the value by one step.
- Home moves to the minimum value.
- End moves to the maximum value.

dolist.text: Use a slider when users benefit from adjusting a value visually within a range.
Choose a step that matches the level of precision users need.
Show the current value while the user is interacting with the slider.
Provide additional context when the minimum and maximum values are not obvious.

dontlist.text: Don’t use a slider when users need to enter an exact value quickly.
Don’t use a slider for a very large range when small differences between values matter.
Don’t use unnecessarily small steps that make the slider difficult to control.
Don’t rely on the handle position alone when users need to understand the exact value.
Don’t use a slider for choosing between a small number of distinct options. Consider radio buttons instead.
